pr_title: boards: Add support for the raspberrypi pico
pr_body:
This PR provides very basic support for the Raspberry Pi Pico board. It continues #33172 by @ioannisg .
It currently supports the boot process and UART, and is able to run the `hello_world` sample.
As this is still very premature, it still lacks a few important features, such as spawning the second core or supporting `west flash`, but it's probably enough so that other people can start using this board with Zephyr and improve this port.
This PR assumes there is a `hal_raspberrypi` module under `zephyrproject-rtos`. Since I don't have permissions to create this repository, I will need someone to do so, so that I can push my local changes.

If anyone wants to run this, I used raspberrypi's fork of openocd together with a JLink adapter to flash. If you're using JLink, make sure to checkout to the `rp2040_jlink` branch of their fork before installing openocd. Flash using this command:
```
openocd -f interface/jlink.cfg -c 'transport select swd' -f target/rp2040.cfg -c "adapter_khz 2000" -c 'targets rp2040.core0' -c 'program build/zephyr/zephyr.elf verify reset exit'
```

Closes #33012

The standard method for pico is to use UF2 upload via the USB interface, enabled using the bootsel pin.

The sdk (rom??) code does expose some basic functions for programming a connected flash device, which AFAIK can be used instead as required, without affecting the ability to use UF2 later.

edit:
When a pico is booted with bootsel active it initialises the usb interface with two endpoints. One of them pretends to be a flash drive. If you connect a pico in this state to a host computer it will see a drive with two files (a text file and another I can't recall). Those files can be read but not modified. If you copy a file with extension .UF2 to the drive (and its crc is valid) the ROM code will flash the contents to the attached flash memory and then auto reset. Writing anything else to the drive is a no-op.

> The standard method for pico is to use UF2 upload via the USB interface, enabled using the bootsel pin.

This request is for the support of RP2040 SoC by the Raspberry Pi foundation. This is a dual core

with a well documented SDK too.

**Describe why you are asking for this support?**
Describe why you are asking for this support instead of contributing it directly to the tree

The reason I am asking for this support is because I am interested in using Zephyr on this chip.
However, I'm not that experienced with porting socs to zephyr, so i would probably need some guidance or help
taking on this task

Also seeing as Arduino, Adafruit and other distributors are creating boards for this soc.

If this is a new board or SoC, please state whether you are willing to maintain the Zephyr support for it if it is included in the main tree
If this SoC were to be included in the main tree i would be willing to maintain the code for it.

**Additional context**
Add any other context or graphics (drag-and-drop an image) about the hardware here.

review_comments: why not `uart_getc`?
Because it calls `uart_read_blocking`, which is blocking
New to Zephr, but is it ok to mix WRITE_BIT (presumably zephyr macro) with gpio_set_xxx (pico-sdk function) in the same context?

`WRITE_BIT` is just a macro for doing the bit shifts and masking required for setting a bit in a 32 bit value. It's setting a bit in `data->int_enabled_mask`, which is a variable used by the ISR. It's not writing to an actual hardware register.
Ahhh, thanks. I understand now.

For the future, the pico internal rom has a function to return the address of the righmost '1' bit (in a few cycles), which could be used to set 'pin' rather than increment it. Would this be faster than increment & test each pin blindly?
Maybe, but I wouldn't tinker with the ROM for a loop that runs ~30 iterations once at startup

the rom-based functions are just as fast (I think) as flash and made visible via the sdk, so no faffing.

I thought this function was being called once for each interrupt, to determine which associated function(s) to call? No?
Sorry, thought that was the pinctrl file. I might look into it in the future. I don't think using the ROM is that easy (the ROM should be added to the linker script, etc.)

why would it need to be in the linker? Is there some need to record the complete footprint of the program unrelated to loading the code into flash? From the user-of-sdk point of view it's just another sdk call (though in fact it's a macro).
`rpi_pico_gpio`
please use a valid `errno`

From `uart.h`:
>  @retval 0 If a character arrived.
 @retval -1 If no character was available to read (i.e., the UART
            input buffer was empty).
you're right, my fault

I'm not liking the mix of multiply, modulus and shift operators here, especially without brackets amid ">> 4 * ".
Why take the address of the status_reg and then dereference it in next stmt as the only use? Couldn't we just read the value?
A comment to indicate what it's doing would be nice, too: "Read the word containing the 4 bit field of events triggered for this pin" or something like that.
This line is based on the pico-sdk implementation: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_rpi_pico/blob/2062372d203b372849d573f252cf7c6dc2800c0a/src/rp2_common/hardware_gpio/gpio.c#L146

While that may make it understandable, it doesn't make it right.

Could you change it to:  
```
statusreg = irq_ctrl_base->ints[pin / 8];
events = (status_reg >> (4 * (pin % 8))) & ALL_EVENTS;
```
i.e. no ref/deref status_reg, brackets around the 4*pin phrase.

Perhaps others have a view, but I think that is much more readable.
Worth a comment to say that gpio_get_all is a pico-sdk function (and it returns the state of all 30 pins so no need to consult 'dev')?

It's really a problem the functions in pico-sdk are not namespaced. It's confusing to read, but even worse, some function names conflict with Zephyr's (such as `adc_init`). That said, I don't think every call to a pico-sdk function should be commentetd. This is driver code, so you should expect to see pico-sdk calls. Commenting every function call would be too verbose in my opinion.
I agree, and it's unfortunate, and I agree not all should or could be commented. But perhaps some can as a hint?
comment note these are pico-sdk headers
What's going on with this file name? It looks a little weird and seems to be very close to autoconf.h, which feels inappropriate.
Originally `pico-sdk` generates this file, and some `pico-sdk` files include it directly, so that name is essential (it ends up in every picosdk file, which makes it useful for workarounds).
Can you please add a source code comment with this information so it doesn't get lost in the PR thread then?
please include Zephyr header that defines `__asm`.

If I understand this correctly, `asm` is not supported with `-std=c99`, so this macro just converts the few instances of `asm` in pico-sdk to the supported format (I should fix the comment above). I couldn't find anything in Zephyr that would do the same, and I prefer not to include extra headers to this file, as it can cause other problems similar to the KHZ/MHZ thing.
nit: headers need to be self-contained, `<autoconf.h>` is missing here
nice to have: interrupt driven version?
Hi @rivimey, can you check my zephyr fork for this and leave some comments about the uart interrupt driven implementation? It is on rpi_pico_working_uart branch.
I'm no expert but I'll have a look. Would it be included as an alternative or a replacement?

Yes @yonsch, you are right. If you have time, check my branch and tell me if it is ok to make a PR with my implementation.

I think this function should probably acknowledge that the analog input channel pins (26..29) are dealt with slightly differently: specifically that to go analog you completely disable digital control of the pins (using function 'null') and then call the 'pico-sdk' function adc_init() on the pin.

While I'm not asking for adc_init to be performed here (it should be in the adc driver) I do think this function should do gpio_init, gpio_set_function, and then conditionall the rest when pin->alt_func is not the 'null' op.  I could be wrong there though.
Analog isn't enabled yet, so it's safer now to set all pins as digital
Worth a comment to say that gpio_set_irq_enabled is a pico-sdk function?
